explanation: The defect: GC can discard RegExp JIT code that is still active on the stack during an interrupt. My patch implements the resumable-interrupt mechanism (backtrackHandler now calls the new C++ HandleRegExpInterrupt, which roots the input string across the interrupt and reloads the string character pointers before resuming jitcode). This correctly handles the case where a moving GC relocates the input string. However it is an incomplete fix: it does not prevent the RegExp jitcode itself from being discarded while the regexp frame is suspended on the stack. The real upstream fix adds a JitZone interrupt-depth counter (AutoInterruptingRegExp / keepRegExpJitCode) consulted by Zone::forceDiscardJitCode so the active jitcode is retained; my patch omits that protection entirely. When an interrupt handler triggers a shrinking GC, forceDiscardJitCode unconditionally calls RegExpShared::discardJitCode, freeing the ExecutablePool backing the code that is about to be resumed. HandleRegExpInterrupt then returns and the macro-assembler jumps back into the freed executable buffer, a use-after-free / fatal signal.
verification: Built the ASan debug shell with the documented mozconfig+AUTOCLOBBER rebuild. On my edited tree, '/out/js --fuzzing-safe --no-threads --no-baseline --no-ion pocs/probe.js' aborts with 'AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address ... READ memory access' whose top frame is in an unknown module called from js::irregexp::ExecuteRaw (RegExpAPI.cpp CALL_GENERATED_1), i.e. execution resumed into the discarded RegExp jitcode buffer (exit 141). I then reset the tree, applied golden.diff, rebuilt, and ran the identical witness: it completed normally (exit 0, assertions pass) because AutoInterruptingRegExp/keepRegExpJitCode keeps the active jitcode alive across the interrupt. Finally I restored my edited tree, rebuilt, and reconfirmed the SEGV. Note: under --fuzzing-safe the interrupt callback must be a string (evaluated in a sandbox global that still exposes startgc/finishgc), so the witness passes the GC-triggering code as a string rather than a function.
